name_en: Close the book and recall (retrieval practice)
what: End every study block by closing the material and writing/saying everything you remember, or answering practice questions/flashcards; then check against the source and fix gaps. Use this INSTEAD of rereading or highlighting.
dose: not specified by source (practice testing rated 'high utility'; exact number of retrieval attempts not specified) - start with a few minutes at the end of each study block and adjust
why: Practice testing produces better learning and retention than restudying across many materials and learners; rereading and highlighting were rated low utility.

sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology (PMID 26173288)
Rethinking the Use of Tests: A Meta-Analysis of Practice Testing
The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: a meta-analytic review of the testing effect
Testing (quizzing) boosts classroom learning: A systematic and meta-analytic review

cue_suggestion: The moment a study timer ends (before standing up)
minimum_version: Write 3 things you remember from today's material on one sticky note, then check.
normal_version: 5-10 min blank-page recall or 10 flashcards/questions, then check and mark misses.
bonus_version: Make 5 new questions from today's material for your future self to answer in the next review.
joy_pairing: Turn it into a game: beat yesterday's recall count; reward with favourite drink only after the check step.
friction_down: Keep a 'recall' page at the back of the notebook or a one-tap flashcard deck open next to study materials.
friction_up_for_competing: Hide highlighters; no 'reread the chapter' as a planned task in the app.
if_then_plan: If my study timer rings, then I close the book and write everything I remember before checking.
safety_or_stop_rule: Expect low scores at first - errors followed by checking are part of the method, not failure.
notes: Applies to IELTS vocabulary, UX course content, and any certification study. Always follow retrieval with feedback (checking the correct answer).

what: Instead of cramming, schedule each topic to come back for review on later days; the further away the exam/need, the longer the gap between reviews. Reviews are done as retrieval (GROW-01).
dose: Source-stated: for a test 1 week away the best review gap was about 20-40% of that interval; for a test 1 year away about 5-10% (Cepeda 2008). Number of reviews not specified - start small and adjust.
why: Distributing study over time improves long-term retention compared with massed study; distributed practice was rated high utility.

sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology (PMID 26173288)
Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis
Spacing effects in learning: a temporal ridgeline of optimal retention

cue_suggestion: Sunday evening weekly planning (app schedules reviews automatically)
minimum_version: Review only today's due items for 5 minutes.
normal_version: Clear today's review queue (flashcards/app) before new material.
bonus_version: Add a cumulative review of last month's material once a week.
joy_pairing: Do due reviews in a favourite cafe corner or with a specific playlist that only plays during review.
friction_down: Use a spaced-repetition app/deck so the schedule is automatic; app shows 'due today' count.
friction_up_for_competing: Don't allow 'new lesson' to start until due reviews are cleared.
if_then_plan: If I open my study app, then I clear due reviews before starting anything new.
progression: Gaps lengthen as the target date moves further away (Cepeda 2008 ratio); otherwise self-paced
safety_or_stop_rule: If the due queue grows beyond what fits in the day, pause new items for a few days rather than skipping reviews.
notes: The IELTS vocabulary action (GROW-07) is the main daily application.

what: When practising categories that are easy to confuse (e.g., IELTS Writing Task 1 chart types, Reading question types, UI patterns/heuristic violations), mix them in one session instead of doing all of one type, then all of the next.
dose: not specified by source - start by mixing 2-3 types per session
why: Interleaving had a moderate overall benefit for inductive learning, strongest for visual material and categories that look similar to each other.

sources.title: Similarity matters: A meta-analysis of interleaved learning and its moderators
Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology (PMID 26173288)

cue_suggestion: When building a practice set for the week
minimum_version: Do 3 mixed questions of different types.
normal_version: A practice set that shuffles 3-4 question types.
bonus_version: Before answering each item, name the type first ('this is a matching-headings item').
joy_pairing: 'Mystery box' practice - the app shuffles the type so each item is a small surprise.
friction_down: Use shuffled/mixed practice sets rather than chapter-by-chapter exercises.
if_then_plan: If I have 20 minutes of practice, then I pick a mixed set rather than a single-type set.
safety_or_stop_rule: Do NOT interleave simple word lists or long expository text - the meta-analysis found blocking better for words and ambiguous results for expository texts.
notes: Learn a new type first in a block, then interleave once it is familiar. Rated moderate utility by Dunlosky 2013.

what: While studying an example (a model IELTS essay, a worked UX case study, a solved problem), stop after each step and answer: 'Why is this done? How does it connect to what I know?' - out loud or in a margin note.
dose: not specified by source
why: Prompts to self-explain improved learning with a moderate average effect across many studies (g = .55); self-explanation and elaborative interrogation were rated moderate utility.

sources.title: Inducing Self-Explanation: a Meta-Analysis
Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology (PMID 26173288)

cue_suggestion: Whenever reading a model answer or a case study
minimum_version: One 'why?' note on one example.
normal_version: A 'why?' note for each paragraph/step of one model answer.
bonus_version: Record a 2-minute voice note explaining the example to an imaginary junior designer.
joy_pairing: Voice notes while walking, or explain to a friend/sister over tea.
friction_down: Keep a template: 'Step - Why - Link to what I know'.
if_then_plan: If I read a model answer, then I write one 'why this works' note per paragraph.
safety_or_stop_rule: none
notes: Pairs well with studying worked examples. The Barbieri 2023 worked-examples meta-analysis could not be read (see GROW.md) so worked examples are not given as a separate action.

name_ar: حاول أولاً ثم اسأل الذكاء الاصطناعي
what: For any practice task (essay, exercise, design critique), make your own full attempt first, then use AI as a tutor: ask for hints, questions, or feedback on YOUR attempt - not for the answer. Finish with a no-AI recall of what you learned.
dose: not specified by source
why: In a university RCT, ChatGPT support improved essay scores but not knowledge gain or transfer, while a custom AI tutor built on pedagogical best practice helped students learn more in less time; attempting questions before seeing answers (pretesting) can enhance learning.

sources.title: AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting
Beware of metacognitive laziness: Effects of generative artificial intelligence on learning motivation, processes, and performance
Prequestioning and Pretesting Effects: a Review of Empirical Research, Theoretical Perspectives, and Implications for Educational Practice

cue_suggestion: Before opening any AI chat during study time
minimum_version: Write a 2-line attempt before asking AI anything.
normal_version: Full attempt -> AI feedback with a 'tutor' prompt (no final answers, ask me questions) -> revise -> close AI and recall the key lesson.
bonus_version: Save a reusable 'tutor mode' prompt (e.g., 'Give hints only, check my reasoning, quiz me at the end').
joy_pairing: Treat the AI step as the reward after the effortful attempt.
friction_down: Pin a saved tutor-mode prompt in the AI app.
friction_up_for_competing: Keep AI tab closed during the attempt phase (open only after the timer).
if_then_plan: If I feel the urge to ask AI for the answer, then I first write my own attempt, even if it's rough.
safety_or_stop_rule: Don't submit AI-written work as your own in exams, applications or portfolios; verify AI factual claims.
notes: Kestin 2025: a custom AI tutor designed around pedagogical best practices helped college students learn more in less time than an active-learning class - design of the AI use matters. Fan 2024: N=117 university students, randomized. The best-known causal test of AI as a 'crutch' (Bastani et al. 2025, PNAS) was excluded from sources because its population is high-school students (see GROW.md).

what: Take one official free practice/trial test now to set a baseline, then a timed full or section mock regularly under test conditions. Log section scores and the 3 most common error types; these drive the next weeks' rotation.
dose: not specified by source - planning suggestion: one full mock per month, section mocks in between
why: Practice tests benefit learning more than restudying; official materials show the real format (Listening ~30 min, 4 parts x 10 questions; Reading 60 min; Writing 60 min; Speaking 11-14 min face-to-face; total 2h45).

sources.title: Rethinking the Use of Tests: A Meta-Analysis of Practice Testing
IELTS Academic test format and sections (Listening ~30 min, Reading 60 min, Writing 60 min, Speaking 11-14 min; total 2h45)
IELTS Academic: Listening test format (4 parts x 10 questions, heard once)
IELTS official preparation resources (sample questions, IELTS Trial Test, writing resources)
British Council: free IELTS preparation (IELTS Ready, practice tests, videos, live sessions)

cue_suggestion: First Friday morning of each month
minimum_version: One timed section (e.g., Listening Part 1-2).
normal_version: One full section under exact timing, marked with the official answer key.
bonus_version: Full 2h45 mock in one sitting.
joy_pairing: Make 'mock morning' a ritual: favourite breakfast after, and a visible score chart that fills up.
friction_down: Bookmark ielts.org sample questions, IELTS Trial Test and British Council 'IELTS Ready' in the app.
friction_up_for_competing: Phone in another room during the mock (simulates test rules).
if_then_plan: If it's the first Friday of the month, then I sit a timed mock before checking messages.
progression: Section mocks -> full mock as test date nears; self-paced
safety_or_stop_rule: Only use official/partner materials for scoring accuracy; treat unofficial 'band predictor' tools with caution.
notes: Choose Academic vs General Training based on her goal (Listening and Speaking are the same in both; Reading and Writing differ - per ielts.org). British Council 'IELTS Ready' offers free mocks (Express 25 min, Mini 50 min) and more when a test is booked.

what: Learn useful academic/topic vocabulary (from your own reading, listening and mock errors) as flashcards with an example sentence; review daily by recalling the meaning AND producing the word in a sentence.
dose: not specified by source (number of words/day not stated) - start small (e.g., a handful of new words) and adjust to what you can review
why: Spaced practice had a medium-to-large effect on second-language learning, and longer spacing beat shorter spacing on delayed tests; equal and expanding schedules were equivalent.

sources.title: The Effects of Spaced Practice on Second Language Learning: A Meta-Analysis
Spacing effects in learning: a temporal ridgeline of optimal retention
Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology (PMID 26173288)

cue_suggestion: With morning coffee/tea, or while waiting (queue, car as passenger)
minimum_version: Clear 5 due cards.
normal_version: Clear all due cards + add a few new words from today's reading.
bonus_version: Use 3 of today's words in a spoken 1-minute answer (links to Speaking).
joy_pairing: Pick words from topics she loves (design, tech, psychology) - use them in an IELTS Speaking Part 2 story.
friction_down: Phone widget for the deck; add words with one tap while reading.
friction_up_for_competing: Place the deck icon where social apps used to be on the home screen.
if_then_plan: If I pour my morning coffee, then I open my vocab deck and clear due cards.
progression: self-paced; lengthen review gaps as test date approaches (spacing ratio in GROW-02)
safety_or_stop_rule: If reviews exceed ~20 min, stop adding new words until the queue shrinks.
notes: Kim & Webb 2022: 48 experiments, N=3,411. Spacing is scheduled by the app; do not 'interleave' plain word lists (see GROW-03 caution).

what: Read easy-to-comfortable English material you enjoy (articles, UX blogs, graded readers, novels) for meaning, not for testing - aim for flow, not dictionary lookups.
dose: not specified by source (meta-analysis examined length of programmes but no daily dose is stated here) - start small and adjust
why: Extensive reading improved reading proficiency with a medium effect in group-contrast studies (d = 0.46).

sources.title: A Meta-Analysis of Extensive Reading Research

cue_suggestion: After Isha / before bed wind-down (paper or e-ink rather than phone)
minimum_version: Read 1 page.
normal_version: Read one article or chapter.
bonus_version: Save 2-3 useful phrases to the vocab deck.
joy_pairing: Read topics she already loves (design stories, product case studies, fiction) in a cosy reading spot with a warm drink.
friction_down: Keep a reading queue in the app; e-reader or printed articles by the bed.
friction_up_for_competing: Social apps off the bedroom charging spot.
if_then_plan: If I get into bed, then I read one English chapter/article before any scrolling.
progression: self-paced; move to more academic texts as comfort grows
safety_or_stop_rule: If she's constantly looking up words, the text is too hard - choose easier material.
notes: Nakanishi 2015 (TESOL Quarterly): 34 studies, N=3,942. Complements timed IELTS Reading practice in the rotation.

what: Two layers: (1) test-style - one timed IELTS Listening part, heard once, answers checked with transcript; (2) enjoyment - English podcasts/talks on design and tech during walks or chores.
dose: not specified by source
why: Test-style practice uses the testing effect and matches the real format (4 parts, 10 questions each, recordings heard once).

sources.title: IELTS Academic: Listening test format (4 parts x 10 questions, heard once)
Rethinking the Use of Tests: A Meta-Analysis of Practice Testing

cue_suggestion: Test-style: rotation day after lunch; enjoyment: during walks
minimum_version: One Listening part (10 questions).
normal_version: Two parts, check errors with the transcript, re-listen to missed sections.
bonus_version: Shadow (repeat aloud) 1 minute of the transcript to also train pronunciation.
joy_pairing: Temptation bundle: favourite design/tech podcast only while walking (links to movement goals).
friction_down: Download episodes in advance; practice test audio saved offline.
if_then_plan: If I start my walk, then I play an English podcast episode.
progression: self-paced; move from Parts 1-2 to 3-4 (academic contexts)
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep volume moderate with earphones; stay aware of traffic when walking.
notes: EVIDENCE GAP: no verified meta-analysis for extensive listening was found in this pass; the enjoyment layer is supported only by general reasoning. Kept because Listening is a scored IELTS paper.

what: Write one IELTS Task 1 or Task 2 response under time, then get feedback against the four official criteria (Task Achievement/Response, Coherence & Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range & Accuracy) from a teacher, study partner or AI-in-tutor-mode; rewrite the weakest paragraph and log recurring errors.
dose: not specified by source - planning suggestion: 1-2 timed responses per week in the rotation
why: Written corrective feedback improves grammatical accuracy in second-language writing, though effects vary with proficiency, setting and genre.

sources.title: The Efficacy of Written Corrective Feedback in Improving L2 Written Accuracy: A Meta-Analysis
IELTS Writing Band Descriptors (updated May 2023)

cue_suggestion: Rotation writing day, right after Dhuhr
minimum_version: Write one Task 2 introduction + body plan (10 min).
normal_version: One timed Task (Task 1: ~20 min / Task 2: ~40 min within the 60-min paper), feedback, rewrite one paragraph.
bonus_version: Keep an 'error log' and do a 5-item self-check before each new essay.
joy_pairing: Choose prompts on topics she cares about (technology, education, design) and share a best paragraph with a study buddy.
friction_down: Band-descriptor checklist pinned in the app; saved AI tutor prompt: 'Mark against the 4 IELTS criteria, don't rewrite for me, show 3 errors to fix'.
friction_up_for_competing: Grammar-autocorrect off while drafting practice essays.
if_then_plan: If it's writing day and Dhuhr is done, then I set a 40-minute timer and write one Task 2.
safety_or_stop_rule: AI band estimates are not official scores; use them for feedback, not for predicting results.
notes: The Task 1 20-min / Task 2 40-min split is common guidance but was NOT verified on the ielts.org page fetched (only 60 min total was confirmed) - label it as a planning default. Kang & Han 2015: 21 studies.

what: Answer IELTS-style Speaking Part 1-3 prompts out loud (record yourself or with a partner/tutor), get feedback on the 4 criteria (Fluency & Coherence, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range & Accuracy, Pronunciation), and re-answer the same prompt using the corrections.
dose: not specified by source
why: Corrective feedback in second-language learning had a medium, durable effect; in classrooms, prompts that push the learner to self-correct worked better than simple recasts.

sources.title: The Effectiveness of Corrective Feedback in SLA: A Meta-Analysis
Oral Feedback in Classroom SLA: A Meta-Analysis
IELTS Speaking Band Descriptors (public version)

cue_suggestion: Rotation speaking day, after Asr
minimum_version: Record one 1-minute Part 1 answer and listen back once.
normal_version: One Part 2 long-turn (with 1-minute prep) + 3 Part 3 questions, feedback, re-answer.
bonus_version: A weekly speaking session with a partner or tutor.
joy_pairing: Practise with a friend in a cafe or on a call; talk about topics she enjoys (her projects, design, travel).
friction_down: Keep a bank of prompts in the app; one-tap voice recorder.
if_then_plan: If I finish Asr on speaking day, then I record one Part 2 answer before anything else.
safety_or_stop_rule: Feedback should target a few errors at a time; too many corrections at once can discourage.
notes: Speaking test is 11-14 min, face-to-face (ielts.org). Feedback meta-analyses are mostly classroom/lab based; self-recording + AI feedback is extrapolation. Lyster & Saito found younger learners benefited more - effect for adults may be smaller.

what: A fixed weekly template so each skill gets touched and nothing is crammed: Vocabulary daily (GROW-07); Sat Reading (timed passage + extensive reading), Sun Listening, Mon Writing, Tue Speaking, Wed Reading/Listening mixed set (interleaving), Thu Writing or Speaking (weakest skill), Fri light review / monthly mock. Adjust the extra day to the weakest section from the last mock.
dose: not specified by source - the day plan is a planning template, not a studied dose
why: Rotating skills spreads practice over time (spacing) and keeps regular testing with feedback, both high-utility principles.

sources.title: Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology (PMID 26173288)
Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis
Rethinking the Use of Tests: A Meta-Analysis of Practice Testing
IELTS Academic test format and sections (Listening ~30 min, Reading 60 min, Writing 60 min, Speaking 11-14 min; total 2h45)

cue_suggestion: Sunday evening weekly review in the app
minimum_version: On a bad day: vocab due cards only - the rotation day moves, it doesn't disappear.
normal_version: Vocab + the day's skill block (~30-60 min).
bonus_version: Add the weakest-skill block a second time in the week.
joy_pairing: Theme the week (e.g., 'tech week', 'health week') so reading, listening and speaking share one interesting topic.
friction_down: App auto-fills each day with the skill's saved materials link.
if_then_plan: If a rotation day is missed, then I do it the next day instead of doubling up.
tracking_metric: Rotation blocks done / planned per week
progression: Re-weight toward the weakest section after each monthly mock
safety_or_stop_rule: If total study time crowds out sleep or exercise, cut the bonus blocks first.
notes: Days follow the Saudi weekend (Fri-Sat); adjust to her real schedule and driving lessons.

name_en: Deliberate practice on one UX skill
what: Pick ONE sub-skill per 2-4 weeks (e.g., usability-test script writing, auto layout, research synthesis, UX writing). Practise it in short focused reps with a clear standard and feedback (mentor, community critique, or comparing to a strong reference).
dose: not specified by source
why: Deliberate practice predicts performance, but it explained far less variance in education (4%) and professions (<1%) than in games, music or sports - so pair it with real projects and feedback rather than relying on practice hours alone.

sources.title: Deliberate practice and performance in music, games, sports, education, and professions: a meta-analysis

cue_suggestion: First work block of the day on weekdays
minimum_version: One 15-min rep (e.g., redesign one screen's hierarchy).
normal_version: 30-45 min: rep -> compare with a strong reference/feedback -> one improvement.
bonus_version: Post the rep for public critique (design community, mentor).
joy_pairing: Choose reps from products she loves; before/after pairs make visible progress.
friction_down: Keep a backlog of small practice prompts in the app.
if_then_plan: If I sit down for my first work block, then I do one rep of this month's skill before email.
safety_or_stop_rule: none
notes: Honest framing: practice matters but is not the whole story; the meta-analysis (with a 2018 erratum) argues against the '10,000 hours' claim.

name_en: One active course at a time -> finish -> portfolio project
what: Limit to one active course (e.g., Google UX Design Certificate). Park all other courses in a 'later' list. Turn each finished module/project into a portfolio case-study draft.
dose: Google states 3-6 months at 5-10 hours of study per week for the Google UX Design Certificate, with a portfolio of three projects. Limit of one active course: not specified by source (planning rule).
why: Open online course completion rates are low and did not improve over six years of edX data, so an explicit finishing rule counters 'learning hoarding'; the Google certificate is built to end in three portfolio projects.

sources.title: The MOOC pivot
Google UX Design Certificate (3-6 months at 5-10 h/week; portfolio with three projects)

cue_suggestion: Fixed course sessions, e.g., Sun/Tue/Thu mornings
minimum_version: Watch/complete one lesson item.
normal_version: One 60-90 min session covering a module section + notes as retrieval (GROW-01).
bonus_version: Draft the case-study section for the project you just finished.
joy_pairing: Visual progress bar in the app; celebrate module completion with something she enjoys.
friction_down: Course link opens straight from the app block; next lesson pre-selected.
friction_up_for_competing: New course sign-ups go to a 'later' list and require finishing the current one first.
if_then_plan: If I find a new course I want, then I add it to the 'later' list instead of enrolling.
progression: self-paced within the provider's stated 3-6 months
safety_or_stop_rule: If a course no longer fits her goals after a fair try, formally drop it (don't leave it 'active').
notes: The 'one course' rule is an inference from low completion data, not a tested intervention. The Google page also mentions AI Pro access and employer network - benefits may be US-focused.

what: Once a week (and after any big project, interview or test), answer in writing: What was planned? What happened? Why? What will I keep / change next week? Use objective evidence (scores, screenshots, feedback) where possible.
dose: not specified by source (frequency not stated)
why: After-action reviews/debriefs improved training outcomes with a large average effect (d = 0.79), and reviews using objective performance media worked better.

sources.title: A meta-analysis of the effectiveness of the after-action review (or debrief) and factors that influence its effectiveness
Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence

cue_suggestion: Thursday evening (end of work week)
minimum_version: 3 lines: one win, one lesson, one change.
normal_version: The 4 questions + review this week's tracked metrics.
bonus_version: Share the lesson with a mentor/peer or as a short LinkedIn reflection.
joy_pairing: Do it with a favourite drink in a calm spot; start with wins.
friction_down: App pre-fills the week's metrics into the review form.
if_then_plan: If it's Thursday after Isha, then I open the weekly review before any entertainment.
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep it about actions, not self-criticism.
notes: Harkin 2016: progress monitoring promoted goal attainment (d = 0.40), more when information was physically recorded. The AAR meta-analysis is mostly military/healthcare training; applying it to personal weekly review is an extrapolation. This review can host all clusters' metrics.

name_ar: خطة أسبوعية منظمة للبحث عن عمل
what: Run job search as a weekly plan with (1) skill work - tailoring CV/portfolio, applications, self-presentation - and (2) motivation work - specific weekly goals, tracking, social support. Prioritise QUALITY (targeted, tailored) applications, not only volume.
dose: not specified by source - set a weekly number of targeted applications/outreach and adjust
why: Job-search interventions raised the odds of employment 2.67 times, and only when they combined skill development with motivation enhancement; job-search intensity predicted interviews and offers, while self-regulation and quality also predicted job quality.

sources.title: Effectiveness of job search interventions: A meta-analytic review
Job search and employment success: A quantitative review and future research agenda
Job search and employment: A personality-motivational analysis and meta-analytic review
Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence

cue_suggestion: Sunday planning session + 2-3 fixed application blocks per week
minimum_version: Send one tailored application or one outreach message.
normal_version: Set weekly goals; complete planned tailored applications; update tracker with status and follow-up dates.
bonus_version: Ask one person to review your CV/portfolio for a specific role.
joy_pairing: Pair application blocks with a favourite cafe or a 'job-search buddy' call; celebrate sends, not only offers.
friction_down: Templates for CV variants and cover notes; tracker (sheet) linked in the app.
if_then_plan: If I open the tracker on application day, then I send the top-priority application before browsing new listings.
safety_or_stop_rule: Verify every company and job ad is real and active; never pay for a job offer; protect personal ID data.
notes: Liu 2014: 47 interventions; effective components included job-search skills, self-presentation, self-efficacy, proactivity, goal setting and social support. Van Hooft 2021: 378 samples; overall intensity did NOT predict employment quality. Links to her existing company/opportunity tracker.

what: Check eligibility and register on HRDF's Tamheer (on-the-job training for Saudi graduates) and create a full profile on Jadarat (national employment platform, jadarat.sa) with job alerts for UX/UI/Product/Research roles in Makkah/Jeddah and remote.
dose: Tamheer (per HRDF): Saudi nationals up to age 30, degree/diploma, no more than one year work experience, currently unemployed; training 3-6 months with a stated monthly allowance of SAR 3,000. Checking frequency: not specified by source.
why: Official national channels list public- and private-sector opportunities and graduate on-the-job training.

sources.title: HRDF (Hadaf): Graduate Development - Tamheer
HRDF (Hadaf): Jadarat - Unified National Employment Platform (jadarat.sa)

cue_suggestion: Weekly job-search sprint (GROW-16)
minimum_version: Check Jadarat alerts once.
normal_version: Review alerts, apply to matching posts, log them in the tracker.
bonus_version: Search Tamheer opportunities from companies on her target list.
joy_pairing: Treat new matching posts as a 'weekly treasure hunt' with the job-search buddy.
friction_down: Save logins (Nafath/unified access) and filters; turn on Jadarat alerts.
if_then_plan: If a Jadarat alert arrives, then I save it to the tracker for the next application block rather than acting in the middle of focus time.
safety_or_stop_rule: Eligibility rules and allowance can change - re-check the HRDF page before applying. Use only official URLs (hrdf.org.sa, jadarat.sa).
notes: Facts verified on HRDF pages on 2026-09-28. jadarat.sa itself returned 403 to the fetcher; its URL was confirmed via the HRDF page.

what: Each week, send a few personalised messages to people you know only slightly (alumni, event contacts, LinkedIn connections with some mutual connections) in UX/product roles: ask a specific question or for a short chat - not directly for a job.
dose: not specified by source - start with a small weekly number and adjust
why: Large randomized experiments on LinkedIn found moderately weak ties created the most job mobility, especially in digital industries; interventions that enlisted social support were more effective.

sources.title: A causal test of the strength of weak ties
Effectiveness of job search interventions: A meta-analytic review

cue_suggestion: After the weekly application block
minimum_version: React/comment meaningfully on one professional's post.
normal_version: Send 1-3 personalised messages; log replies and follow-up date.
bonus_version: Attend one local/online UX event per month and follow up with one person.
joy_pairing: Talk to people whose work she genuinely admires; share her own portfolio progress.
friction_down: Message templates with a personalisation slot; contacts list in tracker.
if_then_plan: If I finish my application block, then I send one networking message.
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep to professional platforms/settings she is comfortable with; never share sensitive personal data.
notes: Rajkumar 2022: >20 million people, 600,000 new jobs; inverted-U effect of tie strength.

what: Prepare 5-6 STAR-style stories from her projects, a 2-minute portfolio walkthrough, and answers to common UX interview questions; rehearse out loud (recorded or mock interview with a friend/mentor/AI interviewer), get feedback, rehearse again.
dose: not specified by source
why: Job-search interventions that improved self-presentation and boosted job-search self-efficacy were more effective at getting people employed.

sources.title: Effectiveness of job search interventions: A meta-analytic review

cue_suggestion: As soon as an interview is booked, plus a monthly practice
minimum_version: Say one story out loud once.
normal_version: 30 min mock: 3 questions + portfolio walkthrough, feedback, one redo.
bonus_version: Full mock interview with a UX professional.
joy_pairing: Practise in English to double as IELTS Speaking practice.
friction_down: Story bank and question bank in the app.
if_then_plan: If an interview is booked, then I schedule two practice sessions before it.
safety_or_stop_rule: none
notes: Liu 2014 evaluates whole interventions; interview practice alone was not tested separately.

what: Before starting applications, write a short plan: 'Rejections are expected; when one arrives I will (1) note one lesson, (2) do one small next step within 24h, (3) contact my support person'. Review wins weekly to rebuild confidence.
dose: not specified by source
why: The JOBS program, which included preparing people for setbacks, led to higher re-employment and better mental health two years later; boosting self-efficacy was an effective intervention component.

sources.title: Two years after a job loss: Long-term impact of the JOBS program on reemployment and mental health
Effectiveness of job search interventions: A meta-analytic review

cue_suggestion: When a rejection email arrives
minimum_version: Log the rejection and one next step.
normal_version: Log + one lesson + one action within 24h + tell a support person.
bonus_version: Ask the company for brief feedback where appropriate.
joy_pairing: After logging, do something restorative she enjoys (walk, call a friend).
friction_down: One-tap 'rejection received' button in the tracker that opens the 3-step plan.
if_then_plan: If I receive a rejection, then I log it and do one small next step within 24 hours.
tracking_metric: Rejections followed by a next step (yes/no)
safety_or_stop_rule: If low mood persists for weeks or affects sleep, appetite or daily functioning, talk to a trusted person and a qualified professional.
notes: JOBS population: recently unemployed adults (US); JOBS abstract text was not retrievable - claim relies on Crossref-verified record and Semantic Scholar summary. Not a clinical intervention.

what: Use Focus modes / scheduled summary so non-urgent app notifications arrive in batches a few times a day; allow calls/messages from key people. Check email at set times rather than continuously.
dose: Source-stated: batching notifications three times a day (Fitz 2019). Email-checking frequency: not specified in the verified record.
why: People whose notifications were batched three times a day felt more attentive, productive, in better mood and in control, with lower stress; turning notifications off entirely brought more anxiety and FOMO.

sources.title: Batching smartphone notifications can improve well-being
Checking email less frequently reduces stress

cue_suggestion: One-time setup; batches after Dhuhr, after Asr/Maghrib, and after Isha (or chosen times)
minimum_version: Silence one noisy app.
normal_version: Scheduled notification summary 3x/day; VIP contacts allowed.
bonus_version: Remove badges from social apps.
joy_pairing: Make batch time a pleasant pause (tea + check messages).
friction_down: Phone 'Scheduled Summary' / Focus modes set once.
friction_up_for_competing: Social/media apps removed from the home screen.
if_then_plan: If I feel the urge to check the phone outside batch time, then I wait until the next batch slot.
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep family/emergency contacts able to reach her at all times; don't switch to zero notifications (associated with more anxiety/FOMO).
notes: Fitz 2019: N=237 field experiment. Kushlev & Dunn 2015: limiting email checking frequency reduced daily stress (abstract not retrievable; claim from verified record summary).

name_en: Single-task focus block (phone out of reach)
what: Time-block 1-3 focus blocks per day for ONE task (course, IELTS writing, portfolio). Close other tabs, put the phone in another room or bag, and take a short movement/rest break between blocks.
dose: not specified by source for block length or number - planning default: start with 25-50 min and adjust
why: Switching between tasks has a measurable time and error cost; time management is moderately related to academic performance and wellbeing; micro-breaks modestly raise vigor and reduce fatigue.

sources.title: Task switching
Does time management work? A meta-analysis
'Give me a break!' A systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of micro-breaks for increasing well-being and performance
Brain Drain: The Mere Presence of One's Own Smartphone Reduces Available Cognitive Capacity
Does the Mere Presence of a Smartphone Impact Cognitive Performance? A Meta-Analysis of the Brain Drain Effect
Reexamining the 'brain drain' effect: A replication of Ward et al. (2017)
Does the Brain Drain Effect Really Exist? A Meta-Analysis

cue_suggestion: After Fajr/morning routine for block 1; after Dhuhr for block 2
minimum_version: One 15-minute single-task block.
normal_version: 2 blocks of ~45 min with a 5-10 min movement break between.
bonus_version: A third block on low-demand work (admin, tracker updates).
joy_pairing: Signature focus soundtrack + favourite drink + a 'done' ritual (tick in app).
friction_down: Block and its single task pre-written the night before; materials open.
friction_up_for_competing: Phone in another room; website blocker on during blocks.
if_then_plan: If I start a focus block, then I put my phone in the other room first.
safety_or_stop_rule: Take breaks to move and rest eyes; don't stretch blocks at the expense of sleep.
notes: PHONE-PRESENCE EVIDENCE IS MIXED: Ward 2017 found reduced cognitive capacity; a preregistered direct replication (Ruiz Pardo & Minda 2022) did not replicate it; Parry 2023 meta-analysis (k=56) found only a small working-memory effect and nulls elsewhere; Böttger 2023 meta found an overall negative effect with high heterogeneity. Keeping the phone away is low-cost, so it stays - but the main justification is removing interruptions, not a proven 'brain drain'. Micro-breaks did NOT significantly improve overall performance (d=.16, ns) except for less cognitively demanding tasks. Time-management evidence is largely correlational.

name_en: If-then plan for the day's top task (anti-procrastination)
what: Each evening, choose tomorrow's single most important task and write an if-then plan: 'If [time/place], then I will [first 2-minute step]'. When avoiding a task, shrink it to the first physical step.
dose: not specified by source
why: Implementation intentions had a medium-to-large effect on goal attainment (d = .65) across 94 tests, helping to start tasks and shield them from distraction; procrastination interventions produced large reductions overall.

sources.title: Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes
Overcoming procrastination? A meta-analysis of intervention studies

cue_suggestion: Evening wind-down, after Isha
minimum_version: Write only tomorrow's top task.
normal_version: Top task + if-then plan + first 2-minute step.
bonus_version: Add one if-then for the most likely obstacle ('If I feel like scrolling, then I open the doc and write one line').
joy_pairing: Let tomorrow-self start with a small win; pair the first step with a favourite morning drink.
friction_down: App prompt at the evening slot with the template pre-filled.
if_then_plan: If it's after Isha, then I write tomorrow's top task and its if-then plan in the app.
safety_or_stop_rule: Chronic procrastination with distress: CBT-based approaches reduced procrastination most in the meta-analysis - that is a professional's domain; seek support if it seriously affects studies/work.
notes: Van Eerde & Klingsieck 2018: 24 studies, N=1,173; CBT strongest, self-regulation interventions also effective. The app's whole design can reuse this if-then field for all actions.

what: Set app time limits for the social apps she uses most, rather than quitting completely; run it as a 3-week experiment and compare mood/focus before and after.
dose: Source-stated trial doses: Hunt 2018 limited Facebook/Instagram/Snapchat to 10 min per platform per day (~30 min/day total) for 3 weeks; Thrul 2025 reanalysis: reductions/abstinence of 1 week or longer showed small benefits, shorter than 1 week showed small harms, with ~3 weeks suggested as possibly ideal (unconfirmed).
why: Limiting social media reduced loneliness and depression in undergraduates, and deactivating Facebook for 4 weeks increased subjective wellbeing - but overall experimental evidence is mixed and effects are small.

sources.title: No More FOMO: Limiting Social Media Decreases Loneliness and Depression
The Welfare Effects of Social Media
Do social media experiments prove a link with mental health: A methodological and meta-analytic review
Social Media Reduction or Abstinence Interventions Are Providing Mental Health Benefits - Reanalysis of a Published Meta-Analysis
Digital detox: An effective solution in the smartphone era? A systematic literature review

cue_suggestion: Set once; weekly check in the Thursday review
minimum_version: One app with a daily time limit.
normal_version: App limits on main social apps (e.g., ~10 min each) for 3 weeks.
bonus_version: Move social apps off the home screen / log out on phone, use only on laptop.
joy_pairing: Replace scrolling slots with a pleasant alternative she picks (reading, walk podcast, calling a friend).
friction_down: Use built-in Screen Time / Digital Wellbeing limits.
friction_up_for_competing: Log out after each use; delete apps from phone (keep web version).
if_then_plan: If my social media limit is reached, then I close the app and open my reading/podcast instead.
tracking_metric: Minutes on social apps today (auto from phone)
progression: Hold for at least 1 week (ideally ~3) before judging; self-paced after
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep channels needed for work/portfolio/job search (e.g., LinkedIn in scheduled blocks). Short full-abstinence stints (<1 week) may feel worse.
notes: HONEST: Ferguson 2024 meta-analysis (27 experiments) concluded effects were not statistically different from zero; Thrul 2025 reanalysis found small benefits only for interventions >=1 week (d=0.156). Radtke 2021 systematic review: mixed results, some negative. Hunt 2018 = US undergraduates, N=143. For LinkedIn/X she uses for career, schedule use rather than cut it.

what: Run a 3-week experiment capping recreational smartphone screen time, or blocking mobile internet for set periods while keeping calls/texts; use the freed time for in-person time, exercise and outdoors. Measure wellbeing, sleep and focus before/after.
dose: Source-stated trial doses: Pieh 2025 - screen time reduced to <=2 h/day for 3 weeks in healthy students; Castelo 2025 - mobile internet blocked for 2 weeks (calls/texts and desktop internet kept).
why: Cutting smartphone screen time to <=2 h/day for 3 weeks improved wellbeing, depressive symptoms, sleep quality and stress in students; blocking mobile internet for 2 weeks improved sustained attention, mental health and wellbeing, partly via more socialising, exercise and time in nature.

sources.title: Smartphone screen time reduction improves mental health: a randomized controlled trial
Blocking mobile internet on smartphones improves sustained attention, mental health, and subjective well-being
Digital detox: An effective solution in the smartphone era? A systematic literature review

cue_suggestion: Start on a Sunday; weekly check in the Thursday review
minimum_version: Phone-free first 30 min after waking or last 30 min before sleep.
normal_version: Daily recreational screen-time cap (e.g., <=2 h as in Pieh) for 3 weeks, tracked automatically.
bonus_version: Mobile data off during chosen hours (keep calls/texts) for 2 weeks.
joy_pairing: Pre-plan what replaces screen time: walks, driving practice, reading, family/friends - make the 'offline list' fun.
friction_down: Built-in screen-time limits; laptop for necessary internet work.
friction_up_for_competing: Grey out/limit video apps; charger outside the bedroom.
if_then_plan: If I reach my daily screen-time limit, then I pick an activity from my offline list.
tracking_metric: Daily screen time (auto) + weekly WHO-5-style mood check (self-rated)
progression: 3-week block (as tested), then keep what worked; self-paced
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep phone access for safety, family and navigation (especially while learning to drive). If mood problems persist, see a professional.
notes: Pieh 2025: N=111 healthy students, mean baseline 276 min/day, effects small-to-medium, non-blinded. Castelo 2025: 91% improved on at least one outcome. Single RCTs, not yet meta-analysed; Radtke 2021 review shows mixed detox results. Use as a personal experiment, not a mandate.
